==English== ===Alternative forms=== * {{alter|en|obtein|obteyn||obsolete}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*ten-}} From {{inh|en|enm|obteinen}}, from {{der|en|xno|obtenir}}, {{m|fro|optiner}} et al., and {{der|en|frm|obtenir}}, from {{der|en|la|obtinēre||to gain, achieve, succeed, possess}}, from {{m|la|ob-}} + {{m|la|tenere|tenēre|to hold}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/əbˈteɪn/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-obtain.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪn|s=2}} * {{homophones|en|abthane}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[get hold of]]; to [[gain#Verb|gain]] [[possession]] of, to [[procure]]; to [[acquire]], in any way. {{defdate|from 15th c.}} #: {{co|en|'''obtain''' permission}} #: {{co|en|'''obtain''' information}} #: {{co|en|difficult to '''obtain'''}} #: {{ux|en|Applicants must '''obtain''' a permit before construction.}} #: {{ux|en|We '''obtained''' accurate data from the survey.}} #* {{RQ:Tyndale NT|Luke|XVIII|text=And a certayne ruler axed him: sayinge: Goode Master: what ought I to do, to '''obtaine''' eternall lyfe?}} #* {{RQ:Austen Mansfield Park|chapter=III|volume=II|page=64|passage={{...}} Julia was quite as eager for novelty and pleasure as Maria, though she might not have struggled through so much to '''obtain''' them, and could better bear a subordinate situation.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[secure#Verb|secure]] (that) a specific [[objective]] or state of affairs be reached. {{defdate|15th–19th c.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1722|author=w:Daniel Defoe|title=w:Colonel Jack |passage=he was condemned to die for the felony, and being so well known for an old offender, had certainly died, but the merchant, upon his earnest application, had '''obtained''' that he should be transported, on condition that he restored all the rest of his bills, which he had done accordingly.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[prevail]], be [[victorious]]; to [[succeed]]. {{defdate|15th–19th c.}} #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|3|2|passage=“O daughter deare!” (said she) “despeire no whit;
For never sore but might a salve '''obtain''' {{...}}.”}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1701|author=w:Jonathan Swift|title=Contests and Dissentions in Athens and Rome |passage=This, though it failed at present, yet afterward '''obtained''', and was a mighty step to the ruin of the commonwealth.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[hold#Verb|hold]]; to [[keep#Verb|keep]], [[possess]] or [[occupy]]. {{defdate|15th–18th c.}} #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Regained|book=1|page=6|lines=76–79|passage=His mother then is mortal, but his Sire
He who '''obtains''' the monarchy of Heav'n,
And what will he not do to advance his Son?}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|especially|philosophy}} To [[exist]] or [[be the case]]; to [[hold true]], be [[in force]]. {{defdate|from 17th c.}} #* {{RQ:London Iron Heel|chapter=17|passage=Even though the Pervaise confession had never come to light, no reasonable doubt could '''obtain'''; for the act in question {{...}} was on a par with countless other acts committed by the oligarchs, and, before them, by the capitalists.}} #* {{RQ:Stephenson Snow Crash|page=460|passage=But the hostage situation no longer '''obtains''', and so Uncle Enzo feels it important to stop Rife now, {{...}}}} ====Conjugation==== {{en-conj|old=1}} ====Synonyms==== * {{sense|to gain possession of}} {{l|en|get}}, {{l|en|gain}}, {{l|en|acquire}}, {{l|en|attain}}, {{l|en|procure}}, {{l|en|exact}}, ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|obtainability|obtainable|obtainer|preobtain|reobtain|unobtainability |obtainment|obtainance|unobtained}} ====Related terms==== {{rootsee|en|ine|ten}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top-see|to get hold of;
